title: Develop
description: A wooden utility pole shot from its foot, straight up through its crossarms and cables into summer cumulus, coming up like a print in a darkroom tray, except that the developer runs through the scene's depth rather than across the paper. It opens as a print does, the darkest, nearest wood first, at the foot of the pole, and climbs it. Drag and a thin band of warm light carries on through the depth; start from a blank sheet on the sky and it runs the other way, from the far sky towards you. Behind it the photograph has arrived, sharp and in full colour. Ahead of it the scene is not there yet: a faint, light latent print in the sky's own blue, out of focus by as much as the depth still to cover, the cloud melting rather than breaking into bokeh, its strata lifted slightly towards you and waiting to settle. In the sky the depth is the cloud's own, so the cores come up first and the front threads the cumulus. Let go and the front carries your speed, then the print settles. Drag back to undo it.
intent: One depth-keyed reveal from herb's CrowdVolt depth research (factory/reality/crowdvolt-depth-heroes.md: a front sweeps a key 0..1 through depth; scan, focus pull, assemble, strata), finished as a title sequence with the quality of a print coming up in a darkroom tray, in the summer-film genre (factory/reality/genre-spec.md). References: Saul Bass's and Pablo Ferro's title sequences that reveal an image by a moving edge (https://www.artofthetitle.com/), and the darkroom print emerging in developer (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Photographic_developer).

sources.author: Dina Lydia (@dinazina)
sources.note: 3593x2736, Seattle, a worm's-eye frame from the foot of the pole: its sides converge on a vanishing point in the upper third of the frame, the cables and braces radiate out of it, cumulus all round. Cropped to a full-width 3:2 band (rows 200-2595) and shipped at 2400x1600. Re-plated from the earlier PJH (@dokae) catenary mast in Ine (unsplash 6DHLBwmRkOw), a 40-degree look up that read as an ordinary snapshot. Depth Anything V2 Small (tools/depth/depth_hr.py), prepared as in herb's notes (percentile normalise, median, dilate near values, slight blur). Split into two layers: the sky with the pole, crossarms, braces and every cable painted out (LaMa, big-lama ONNX, at half size through a mask dilated well past the silhouettes, matched to the sky round each hole in log light, grain put back; shown only a few pixels past the structure, the photo's own sky beyond), and the structure as a known-background matte over it (alpha = (I-B).(F-B)/|F-B|^2; cables found by a black-hat on luma; the bright hardware, lit braces and insulators, found as narrow features lighter or darker than the local sky that hang off the structure, and matted against the painted sky; the matte is pulled against a log-light normalised-convolution fill). The sky key's distance term is measured from the zenith the pole points at, and the sky is graded round it in the bake, in log light: deep cobalt overhead opening to a paler cyan at the corners, the cloud's rims turned off lilac to a cyan-grey and its tops warmed to a neutral. Bake: tools/depth/bakes/develop/bake.py.
